summary:
Hawaii is a state of the United States and stands under the US federal framework; the national record carries federal law, passport rules and entry screening. The findings below concern Hawaii's own statutes and their application.

A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment, built from a rubric applied to thousands of tracked anti-trans bills covering youth-care bans, bathroom bans, birth-certificate and driver-licence restrictions and the withdrawal of legal recognition, places Hawaii in a fifteen-state Most Protective tier and describes the laws of that tier as having gone above and beyond in safeguarding transgender rights. The assessment is a rubric-based ranking of legislation rather than a measure of enforcement.

Hawaii holds a healthcare shield law or executive order, recorded as current on 27 September 2026, which protects patients and providers from civil or criminal charges where care that is lawful in Hawaii was banned in the patient's home state. For a trans visitor travelling from a state with a youth-care ban or another care restriction, this is the provision most directly relevant to obtaining care while in Hawaii.

State law prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity or expression in housing and public accommodations since 2005 and 2006, in employment since 2011, in insurance contracts since 1 July 2016, and in jury selection under legislation signed in June 2022 and effective 1 January 2023. The same 2022 legislation created a state LGBTIQ+ commission and mandated state health insurance coverage for sexual reassignment surgery.

The hate-crime statute covers actual or perceived gender identity or expression, defined to include a person's actual or perceived gender, gender identity, gender-related self image, appearance or expression, whether or not it differs from that traditionally associated with the person's sex at birth. The gay and trans panic defences were abolished by a bill passed in April 2019, signed on 26 June 2019 and effective immediately.

Changing a gender marker on state documents does not require surgery. Since a law passed on 5 May 2015, signed 14 July 2015 and effective immediately, transgender people may change the marker by request; an updated birth certificate requires a completed Application for Amendment to Birth Record and an affidavit from a licensed physician, and an updated driver's licence or state ID requires a Gender Designation Form completed by a medical or social professional confirming gender identity. An X sex option on driver's licences and birth certificates, passed in May 2019, signed 26 June 2019 and effective 1 July 2020, is available by request with no medical documentation required.

Health insurance provisions include coverage of sex reassignment surgeries under the 2016 insurance nondiscrimination rule, mandatory coverage effective 1 January 2023, and the inclusion of transgender individuals in health insurance planning under a bill passed in May 2022 with an emergency clause signed a month later and effective immediately, replacing male-only and female-only planning in place since 1980. Conversion therapy on minors has been banned since 1 July 2018.

Marriage is open to couples regardless of gender under the Hawaii Marriage Equality Act, passed by the Senate 20-4 on 30 October 2013 and by the House 30-19 on 8 November 2013, given final Senate approval 19-4 on 12 November 2013 and signed on 13 November 2013, with marriages beginning 2 December 2013. The 1998 constitutional amendment that authorised the legislature to reserve marriage to opposite-sex couples was repealed by referendum on 5 November 2024, with 55.94 per cent voting to delete the opposite-sex limitation from Article I Section 23. Reciprocal beneficiary relationships have existed since 1997, civil unions were signed on 23 February 2011 and effective 1 January 2012, and benefits for the partners of state employees have been provided since 1997.

Parentage rules have moved toward gender neutrality. A bill passed in April 2021 and signed in July 2021 recognised unmarried same-sex parentage with immediate effect, and Act 298, effective 1 January 2026, implements gender-neutral parentage by voluntary acknowledgment or court adjudication.

Consensual same-sex sexual activity has been lawful since the 1972 repeal took effect in 1973, replacing an 1850 anti-sodomy statute; the age of consent has been 16 regardless of gender or sexual orientation since 2001.

The national inventory of bathroom restrictions does not list Hawaii among the nine states and one territory that bar transgender people from sex-segregated facilities in schools or government buildings.
tangentialFactors:
The July 2026 assessment's lowest tier is characterised by prison terms of up to five years for gender-identity-related offences and by arrest policies for bathroom use, which sets the contrast against Hawaii's placement in the Most Protective tier.

Hawaii's marriage law has a longer contested history. The state Supreme Court found the opposite-sex marriage restriction unconstitutional in May 1993; the legislature enacted a statutory ban in 1994; Constitutional Amendment 2 passed in November 1998 with 70 per cent support, permitting a legislative ban that was later dismissed in court; the amendment was repealed in November 2024.

The 1850 anti-sodomy statute punished consensual adult conduct, heterosexual and homosexual alike, with up to 20 years' hard labour and a $1,000 fine, and was last enforced in the 1958 case Territory v. Bell. Repeal came in April 1972, effective at the start of 1973, with the sex offences code revised in 1986; the age of consent was lowered to 14 in 1986 regardless of gender or sexual orientation and raised to 16 in 2001.

The federal layer, including passport markers, entry screening and federal custody rules, is set out in the national record and applies in Hawaii as elsewhere in the United States.
localsOnly:
Residents' protections extend to schools and public institutions. An anti-bullying law covers gender identity and expression, including cyberbullying, in public elementary and secondary schools, and a July 2018 education-equity law effective 1 January 2019 ensures students are not denied programmes or extracurricular activities because of sexual orientation or gender identity.

Discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation has been prohibited in employment since 1991, in housing since 2005 and in public accommodations since 2006, and the hate-crime statute covers actual or perceived sexual orientation. A state LGBTIQ+ commission established in 2022 works on equal treatment.

Family formation is open on several routes: adoption by same-sex couples, IVF and artificial insemination for lesbian couples with the non-genetic, non-gestational mother recognised if married, and surrogacy, with courts ruling in favour of gay male gestational surrogacy.

State employee benefits for partners have been provided since 1997, alongside reciprocal beneficiary relationships created in 1997 and civil unions effective 1 January 2012.
outOfScopeNotes:
The healthcare shield law is recorded as existing, but the sources do not describe how a visitor invokes it, what documentation is required, or whether it covers care arranged before arrival.

No Hawaii-specific figures on anti-trans violence, hate-crime charges or prosecutions appear in the inventory, so no assessment of enforcement intensity can be made from these sources.

The July 2026 ranking is a rubric applied to tracked legislation; it does not measure how agencies, police or health providers act in practice.

Whether the state X marker on licences and birth certificates remains available in practice alongside the federal passport marker restrictions is not addressed by the sources.
